clue.text: Reflective plastic penis – very English

indicators.note: something plastic can be moulded into any shape, so these letters are remoulded

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
V is the standard abbreviation for very
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A smutty remark about a shiny plastic sex toy, with an aside that it is terribly English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reflective' seems to describe the plastic's shine, but it is the definition, meaning thoughtful.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone reflective is lost in thought, deeply musing, which is the sense of the adjective here.

clue.text: Lapse of Times power in Ireland

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it, so these letters go within the outer word

blocks.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as 'times'
P is the symbol for power in physics
Eire is the Irish-language name for Ireland

explanation.surface: A slip-up by The Times newspaper about who holds power in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper, but it is the multiplication sign X.
explanation.definitionFit: A licence or subscription that lapses runs out at the end of its term, so the verbs match.

clue.text: A quick bonk – but slow to get over it

blocks.note: speed is quickness; read loosely, a quick one
hump is slang for sex, as bonk is

explanation.surface: A hasty sexual encounter that takes a long time to recover from emotionally.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about getting over a fling; the definition means physically driving over a bump in the road. Bonk and hump are both British slang for having sex.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised strip across a road forces drivers to brake, so it is a thing you must slow down to cross.

clue.text: Man turned up TV, taking the piss

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning something up flips it to read from bottom to top
to take something in is to hold it, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: taken as written
piss is British slang for beer, especially weak beer

explanation.surface: Someone cranks up the television volume while mocking the people watching it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking the piss' is British for mocking, but here it means holding the beer. 'Man' is the old sense of a manservant.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentleman's personal manservant is his valet, and 'my man' was the traditional way of naming that servant.

clue.text: Fool needs time back on social media

indicators.note: going back means travelling the opposite way, so the letters read right to left

blocks.note: a twit is a silly person
T is the abbreviation for time
re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: An idiot needs to spend time back on social media again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' looks like part of the phrase 'back on', but it supplies RE, which is then turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: The microblogging site, since renamed X, was one of the best-known platforms of online networking.

clue.text: Game with wank initially (tool pear shaped)

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is kept
going pear-shaped is British slang for going wrong, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A crude joke about a sex act going wrong, with the anatomy turning pear-shaped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tool' reads as slang for penis, but its letters join 'pear' as raw material for the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a team sport played in a swimming pool, with players throwing a ball into a goal.

clue.text: Tries made when England's number one leaves balls

indicators.note: number one is whatever comes first, so only the opening letter is meant
whatever leaves is no longer present, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
testes are testicles, slang balls

explanation.surface: A rugby report: tries were scored after England's star player left the field, with 'balls' as a smutty twist.
explanation.walkthrough: The rugby picture makes 'Tries' look like scores, but it means attempts or trials, and 'number one' is just the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A try is an attempt or trial, as in giving something a try, so tries are experiments or checks.

clue.text: Tip: bad blood hazard

blocks.note: the tip of something is its end
bad blood is hostility or ill feeling

explanation.surface: A warning label: infected blood is a biohazard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hazard' reads as a noun on a warning sign, but it is the verb meaning to put at risk.
explanation.definitionFit: To hazard something is to risk or imperil it, the same verb sense as putting it in danger.

clue.text: Turning purple, I'm having sex – the maximum!

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written
it is a coy word for sex

explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning purple' looks like a flushed face, but 'Turning' just shuffles the colour's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceiling or cap that cannot be exceeded is the highest permitted level, the most allowed.

clue.text: Wonder about Midge as possibly the only means of getting rid of Covid?

definitions.text: possibly the only means of getting rid of Covid?

blocks.note: a miracle is a wonder
C is short for circa, Latin for about
Midge Ure is a Scottish musician, singer with Ultravox and co-organiser of Live Aid

explanation.surface: Someone muses about whether only a miracle could end the pandemic, mentioning a pop star along the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Midge' looks like a tiny insect, but it is the singer Midge Ure. The question mark marks the definition as a wry comment written in 2020, before vaccines.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy that works astonishingly well is called this, and in 2020 many joked only such a wonder would end the pandemic.

clue.text: Trump, ultimately missing out on award: "Feel bitter"

something missing out is absent, so that letter is left out of the word

explanation.walkthrough: Trump's name supplies only its last letter, which is then taken out of the gift.
explanation.definitionFit: To begrudge something and harbour indignation about it is to hold a grudge, a sour grievance.

clue.text: (& 18ac.) Trump's recent political choice? Unstable eurosceptic (he met just four) ...

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder

clue.text: Doctor may bless a load of parliamentarians?

clue.text: see 14ac.
Remove Davey – to be dumped in Channel

indicators.note: something dumped in a place is dropped inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: Ed Davey is leader of the Liberal Democrats

explanation.definitionFit: To deduct is to subtract or take away an amount, matching the verb remove in the sense of taking off.

clue.text: see 24ac.

clue.text: Play a waiting game on developing Covid symptom?

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to endure anxiety until a situation resolves; literally, a fever makes the body break into perspiration.
